text:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiny proxy middleware that stamps a signed consent assertion on outgoing resident-write requests. goal: let edge short-circuit policy checks without a roundtrip to control-plane for the hot path.

Jordan: can you sketch the token format and verification model? who holds keys?

Sam: short sketch: header `X-Consent-Assertion: <b64jwt>`; JWT-like claims: tenant_id, op (read/write), allowed_regions, nonce, iat, exp. Signed by control-plane using KMS-backed private key. proxies cache public keyset (JWKS-style) and verify locally. tokens TTL ~3-8s to limit exposure.

Maya: what about partial consents (e.g., tenant allowed in eu-west and us-east but not ap-south)? does the proxy need to understand region semantics?

Sam: claim contains allowed_regions array. proxy compares local region id against allowed_regions and either allow short-circuit or trigger fallback. proxies don't need policy rules beyond region membership check and signature validity.

Oliver: fallback behaviour options? forward to primary, request a re-issue, or fail-fast with retry hint?

Sam: we discussed three: (1) forward-to-primary (adds RTT but preserves client success), (2) token-broker hop to get new assertion (adds a hop), (3) 409 with client retry hint for background/non-critical ops. leaning toward forward-to-primary for critical paths.

Priya: SRE + compliance will want observability: counts of rejects, forwards, token-verify failures, and a per-tenant audit trail for consent asserts.

resilience-bot: canary report: prototype middleware with local verification: resident-write median P95 +10ms vs baseline; when token absent or invalid and we forward to primary, observed additional +125ms tail. rejection rate in a small canary (10k reqs) = 0.05% (mostly clock skew).

Jordan: key rotation / rollover notes: prefer rolling keys with dual-signing window (old+new) for ~60s to avoid bursts. publish JWKS endpoint and healthcheck: `/internal/consent-keys`. recommend rotate quarterly, but allow emergency rotate.

Maya: clock skew looks like a real source of rejects. we should have small slack in verification (e.g., allow -2s to +2s skew) and monitor rejected-by-expiry metric.

Oliver: long-term: don't make every proxy responsible for crypto forever. define a lightweight gRPC residency-policy service: ValidateToken(token) -> {allow: bool, reason: string, effective_regions: []}. proxies can call it in medium/large deployments and fallback to local verification in the tiny edge case.

Sam: plan: short-term = middleware stamps header + proxies verify locally (fast rollout); medium-term = residency-policy gRPC service + migrate validation off proxies; long-term = enrich audit events in control-plane.

Jordan: also add a feature-flag gate `residency_local_validation` so we can flip to remote validation or disable local checks if we hit perf regressions during canary.

Priya: for the audit trail: include token_id claim (nonce) and log token validation outcomes (accept/reject/forward) with tenant_id and region in a dedicated telemetry stream (low-volume aggregator). we can keep payloads small.

Sam: Oliver, can you prototype the middleware + add header spec in a PR? also include a tiny `X-Consent-Version: v1` header so we can evolve format.

Oliver: yes. will open PR by end of week. header spec snippet I'll add to the PR: `X-Consent-Assertion: <base64jwt>`

resilience-bot: scheduled chaos test: 2024-12-03 09:00 UTC. scenarios: clock skew +/-5s, keyset mismatch, dropped token-broker responses, high QPS with token cache priming.

Jordan: action items: (1) Oliver prototype PR for middleware + local verifier, (2) Jordan write key-rotation and JWKS health endpoints doc, (3) Priya + SRE define metrics/alerts: token_reject_rate > 0.1% alert, forward_latency_p95 threshold, (4) Sam to draft RFC addendum about opt-in canary rollout and opt-out feature flag.

Maya: +1. keep canary tiny (1-2% of traffic) and monitor cost/latency.

Sam: captured. I'll link follow-up doc in the PR and drop a short runbook for rollback. thanks all.
